bounds: One runtime and at most two recovery starts, all five registration states, optional registered instance, catch/finally interleavings, first and second cooldown intervals. Logical ticks represent whole initial backoff intervals.
fairness: AttemptsSettle assumes fair completion of the host service-load promise and fair processing of finally. Permanent provider/storage stalls do not promise completion.
limitations: Concurrent replacement of the registered class during an unsettled recovery and separate runtime identity maps require the service lifecycle ownership model.
Only the first two exponential delays are represented. Wall-clock rollback, later capped delays, and exceptions thrown by diagnostic observers are outside this domain.
The existing 69-test real runtime/SQLite conformance suite covers hydration failure, recovery deduplication and immediate backoff. It is scenario conformance, not exhaustive schedule equivalence.
